newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak shares steady, SAX boosted by gains to VSZ.
newsitem.headline: Slovak shares steady, SAX boosted by gains to VSZ.

text.p: Moderate gains to steel maker VSZ on Wednesday pushed the Bratislava Stock Exchange's (BSE) 16-share SAX index 0.53 points higher to 169.38.
VSZ closed up 17 crowns at 650, trading 157 shares, the biggest volume of the session on the BSE's listed floor.
"Volumes are still desperately low, but we already are seeing some modest signs of increasing interest (from investors)," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
"However, it's hard to expect that these (signs) would break the current silence on the market," he added.
Oil refinery Slovnaft and oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade. Commercial bank VUB closed unchanged at 1,450 crowns, but traded only 16 shares.
Overall volume eased to 981,545 shares, from 1,142,800 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover decreased to 1.081 billion crowns, from 1.274 billion.
Wednesday's volume and turnover on the BSE were boosted by several direct deals.
